3.5 Hydraulic Cylinder Process Equipment Design and Use
3.5.1 Significance of Adopting Process Equipment for Cylinder Bore Machining

Professional cylinder manufacturers produce internal bore grinding, cold rolling, honing of seamless steel pipes or per JB/T 11718-2013 (Hydraulic Cylinder Barrel Technical Conditions) specified cylinders. Commonly, hydraulic cylinder manufacturers use these cylinders for hydraulic cylinder body manufacturing. For single piece and small batch hydraulic cylinder barrel manufacturing, this has the advantages of being fast, convenient, and low cost. It has been widely used in recent years.

CNC controlled lathe machine tools use combined tool holders for machining (turning and rolling) cylinders that can also be called hydraulic cylinder barrels. In cylinder manufacturing, except for the seamless steel pipe bore that has already been finished, the outer surface, both ends, and the two end face machining (generally only requiring outer surface machining) is performed. The cylinder barrel and cylinder bottom, cylinder head, and other connections (including press-fitting welding, etc.) also require machining. Therefore, at least secondary machining is required to achieve the various design requirements of hydraulic cylinder barrels, including process requirements.

The above-mentioned internal bore drilling, cold rolling (or hot rolling), seamless tube hydraulic cylinder body is a finished or semi-finished product, collectively referred to as the cylinder barrel.

In order to achieve quality assurance for each cylinder bore hole during secondary machining, the straightness, roundness, and several geometric accuracy requirements need to be guaranteed. In practice, one common method is to machine the cylinder barrel outer surface while on the lathe, and then use the outer surface to support the bore through center support and outer clamping for further machining of the cylinder barrel outer frame. This is an important process requirement for the cylinder barrel, but if the cylinder barrel is not used for machining the outer barrel, and subsequent processes are then carried out, this would have been completed. However, it is not satisfactory because the bore machining requirement is also added, and it reduces the cylinder barrel's simplicity. Therefore, many users require the cylinder barrel to have no deformation allowed for secondary machining, which actually limits the user's needs.

It is also mentioned that there can be a challenge in requiring the simultaneous determination of the alignment of both bore ends with the center of the machine tool's center line, thus making it even more difficult. There are two fitting methods, and all methods have a common characteristic where one end is a straight line connection, otherwise another end cannot achieve the alignment. The fitting/assembly must not cause bore deformation or damage. The wire connection fitting's resistance and its external force capability can be quite limited. To improve the anti-vibration capability and other capabilities, it is common practice to first add a processing front end, then use a tail frame to provide support for the cylinder barrel, and then process by removing this section of front end material. Adding a processing front end to the cylinder barrel outer wall also poses the same problem; the section of front end material should not cause the bore to deform. The connection method for this section is critical.

There is also a type of fixed-length mandrel expansion-type cylinder bore inner hole, and the issue is that after clamping, the bore at several hole locations may be damaged. The same issue requires that the mandrel must also have a certain length fixed-length mandrel, and questions arise about how to address this. The process tool provides a one-type vehicle-mounted fixed-length mandrel clamping process equipment. This equipment can utilize a card disk expansion type cylinder barrel for single end clamping. The process tool design requirement for the cylinder barrel section is not to require machining of the outer surface. That is, without using the cylinder barrel outer surface for machining processing, the outer wall equivalent sections are then machined again for further processing. Rather, the direct process tool can achieve the cylinder barrel's usage as one type (a fixed-type mandrel) and can be reused.

The process tool fixed-type mandrel approach to this type of process equipment can guarantee product quality and reliability. It can also serve as the equivalent equipment for quality assurance purposes. However, due to the need for increased production volume and expanded production scale, under the condition of not reducing product quality, such as the company's RAS system cylinder barrel process tool machine tool, the main machine does not allow all cylinder barrel inner diameter bore to be machined. The process tool base standard method makes regulations, and commonly uses the bore diameter of the inner wall for fixation or the straightness standard, which is not possible. In practice, the process tool's choosing approach for the cylinder barrel is required. For another cylinder barrel inner bore center position deviation, screw thread pattern, there exists a certain degree of position deviation. Using this technique, the cylinder barrel must also undergo a further precision machining step, and its cylinder barrel's specifications would also need to meet certain standards, which is not possible. Therefore, the cylinder barrel process tool (specifically the process fixtures used for this particular process equipment) is needed.

Hydraulic cylinder bore honing - how to select process parameters and honing effects. This involves some honing mechanisms that are not very clear. The main issue is the honing cross-hatch angle, but the problem is that some hydraulic cylinder manufacturers commonly need to consider the design and manufacturing of liquid cylinder honing - a further test.

Honing is a finishing process tool that uses a workpiece surface to first apply pressure, then the honing tool simultaneously rotates and reciprocates in the axial direction. The cutting process reduces the workpiece surface by a small amount of precision finishing, belonging to a type of precision grinding. The honing principle is that at a certain pressure, the abrasive grains and the workpiece surface produce a relative combination of contact, and the machining surface cutting generates a cross-hatched and non-repeated complex network pattern, which reduces the wear marks on the surface and produces good lubrication for oil retention.

Honing is divided into three stages: the first stage is the rough cutting stage; the second stage is the crushing and cutting stage; the third stage is the smooth finishing stage (equivalent to polishing). Honing is divided into constant pressure honing and fixed honing.

Honing can change the bore dimensions including: roundness, straightness, cylindricity, and surface roughness. For medium-to-large diameter hydraulic cylinder bores, honing is the most cost-effective, efficient, and reasonable choice.
Honing has the following characteristics:

items: Abrasive grinding load is light, abrasive usage time is long.
Speed is low, generally below 100mm/min.

During honing, attention must be paid to injecting a large amount of cutting fluid, which can remove dislodged abrasive and metal debris in a timely manner. The workpiece surface should be fully separated, with workpiece heating minimized and surface deformation reduced, thus achieving high precision in the workpiece for several positions.

sections.text: Honing can generally achieve IT6-IT7 precision grade bores, with Ra 0.025-Ra 0.2 μm, and form error generally not exceeding 0.005mm.

The process requirements for honing mainly include: honing cross-hatch count, workpiece pressure, honing force, grinding and exceeding outer dimensions, abrasive type and grain size, honing speed, etc.
1) Rotational speed is generally v_r = 14-48m/min, reciprocating advance
Speed v_s = 5-15m/min, cross-hatch angle α = 2arctan(v_s/v_r), cross-hatch angle is generally 30°-60°, with 45° being preferred.
Honing working pressure is selected based on rough and fine honing time of 0.5-1MPa, fine honing pressure of 0.2-0.8MPa, super-fine honing pressure of 0.05-0.1MPa, generally 0.2-0.5MPa.

The honing head when honing must extend beyond the bore at both ends. This common term is called 'overtravel' length. Some materials refer to the cutting length ratio of overtravel to bore length as 1/3 to meet requirements.

items: Suitable abrasives for honing cast iron and non-ferrous materials include silicon carbide type A (GZ) and corundum MA (GW); for honing steel, the ceramic bonded abrasive type is K-P, with abrasive grain size around 180 mesh.

Using constant-pressure honing technique, with two-phase reverse processing, first with rough grinding followed by fine grinding, forming a pattern with a certain depth and consistent cross-angle angle, and retaining a certain depth of grooves.
